Six months before our first production run, our team sat in a rented office reviewing packaging proofs. The preliminary design for Purity Beans Bold featured a clever descriptor that sounded professional but obscured what was inside the jar. It was standard industry practice. It was safe.

Then our operations lead spoke up. He dropped a grocery store jar onto the table—a competitor brand with 'coffee blend' in bold letters and chicory buried in six-point type at the bottom. 'If we hide behind marketing words,' he said, 'we are no different from the noise we set out to fix.'

We scrapped the proof that afternoon. We redesigned every label to be brutally plain. When buyers pick up Purity Beans Bold, they see agglomerated pure coffee with zero chicory. When they check Purity Beans Purista, they see freeze-dried gourmet Robusta granules with zero chicory. When they pick up Purity Beans Ultra Blend, our front label states it is a smooth 70% coffee and 30% chicory milk coffee—no hidden asterisks, no small print.

Building an honest FMCG brand means taking the harder route: absolute transparency over convenient ambiguity. If you manage retail inventory or FMCG distribution and want to stock a brand that refuses to hide its ingredients, message me directly.

blog_post.body:
## What does freeze-dried instant coffee mean for an Indian kitchen?

Freeze-dried instant coffee means the brewed liquid was frozen solid and the ice turned directly into vapor, leaving behind dry granules that never saw high heat. In an Indian kitchen, that translates to a cup that keeps the origin character of the bean instead of tasting like burnt toast. You smell caramel and chocolate notes the moment the jar opens, and they survive the boil of a stovetop milk coffee just as well as a quick black pour-over. A concrete tip: use water just off the boil — around 93–95°C — and stir gently for ten seconds; the granules dissolve cleanly without the clumps you get from spray-dried powders. Purica (pure Arabica, ₹559 for 100 g) and Purista (pure Robusta, ₹509 for 100 g) are the two freeze-dried jars from Purity Beans; both are zero chicory. Bold is agglomerated pure coffee, and Ultra Blend is 70 % coffee with 30 % chicory for drinkers who want a familiar, milder daily cup. Prima is a premium agglomerated Arabica and is not freeze-dried. Pick the jar that matches how you actually drink coffee at home.

### A plain definition

Whatever brought you here, the label settles it. The other single jars on this page are 0% chicory.

## How do you read the chicory line on the jar?
